newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to press ahead with fuel imports.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to press ahead with fuel imports.

text.p: State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) will continue importing fuel despite increasing crude oil allocations to domestic refineries, a senior state oil official said on Tuesday.

Haruna Abubakar, managing director of the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC), a subsidairy of the NNPC, told reporters that the military government had increased the amount of crude allocated to local refineries to 320,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 250,000 bpd.

"But there is a limit to what the refineries can produce in relation to the national demand, so we will still honour our commitment to import fuel for the second part of the year to build up stocks," he said.
"We will like to achieve at least 20-day stock holdings of petroleum products up from the 10-day level now," he added.

Of the new crude allocation for domestic consumption, 220,000 bpd is given to the two refineries in Port Harcourt and the one in Warri, while 100,000 bpd is sent for offshore processing and imported back into Nigeria.
Nigeria placed orders for 33 cargoes of fuel in June to September. Each cargo comprises 33,000 tonnes of gasoline.
The imports followed weeks of acute fuel shortage when business activities and transport in Africa's leading oil producer was paralysed.

Since then the government has said it would try to repair the four local refineries, which together have an installed capacity of 445,000 bpd but produce at a fraction of that because of breakdowns and lack of maintenance.
State radio reported on Tuesday that the government had contracted France's Total SA to run the Kaduna refinery in the north for three years in an effort to end the continual fuel shortages.
It said the contract valued at between $160 million and $220 million, included the cost of the turnaround maintenance of the plant.
